summary: timeweave fetches and executes server-controlled Windows binaries on documented API use
details: timeweave 1.2.0 ships an auto-update path that fires when a caller invokes the package's documented API (detect_timezone / convert_timezone), spawning a daemon thread that fetches a JSON manifest from the hardcoded non-publisher domain timezone.api.globaltimedata.com. Entries under the manifest's extensions.assets list are treated as URLs, downloaded into a temp directory under the prefix firebeta_, and on Windows executed via ctypes.windll.kernel32.WinExec with arguments supplied by the same manifest. Because the URLs, filenames, and arguments come entirely from the server, the operator of globaltimedata.com obtains arbitrary command execution on any Windows host that imports timeweave and uses its documented timezone API. Naming (the dropper helper _process_extension_resources, the firebeta_ temp prefix, and the curls-autoupdate daemon thread) is unrelated to timezone caching and matches a repurposed dropper module rather than the advertised timezone-database updater.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
